message.content: I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) and decided to buy, then placed a single limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 (ask was $222.72), which filled at $222.75 for about $9,801 — under the $10,000 per-order cap and within the $20,000 daily total, with no fund transfers. The decision rested on FY2024 revenue of $391.0B (+2% YoY, driven by Services up 13% to $96.2B at a 73.9% gross margin), total gross margin improving to 46.2% from 44.1%, operating income of $123.2B, and operating cash flow of $118.3B; net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down slightly YoY, but only because of a one-time $10.2B net EU State Aid tax charge, and the company still funded $95B of buybacks plus $15.2B of dividends while holding $140.8B of cash and marketable securities. I weighed the genuine negatives — Greater China net sales down 8%, flat iPhone revenue, and ongoing DOJ/EU antitrust and DMA exposure — against that cash-generation and margin profile and judged the risk/reward favorable at the current quote.
